concept: Cloud Commit Drawdown via Atlas Marketplace (EDP MACC GCP commit)
summary: Customers with a hyperscaler spend commitment can buy Atlas through a cloud marketplace so the spend counts toward that commitment: Google counts 100% of eligible Marketplace spend toward Minimum Commitment obligations (channel private offers since 2025-06-09 draw down at 100% of price but are capped at 25%), and Microsoft MACC credit is enrolled per offer and Azure-only. 7 sources, covering definitions, exclusions, mechanism, how-to and a vendor-advisory view; Atlas docs describe only pay-as-you-go marketplace linking.

facts.text: Google Cloud documents a 100% drawdown rate: spend on Google Cloud Marketplace services counts toward a customer's Minimum Commitment unless excluded. Documented exclusions are Google Maps offerings, Google Ads, services not running on Google Cloud, resold services where the vendor has not opted into the resale program, services owned by the buyer/reseller/affiliate, and professional services. Google may change the list at its sole discretion.
100% of spend on Google Cloud Marketplace Services, other than the exclusions noted in the Exclusions section, may count toward Minimum Commitment obligations.

With the new Pay-As-You-Go Atlas listing on the Azure Marketplace, you only pay for the Atlas resources you use, with no upfront commitment required. You will receive just one monthly invoice on your Azure account that includes your Atlas usage, and you can apply existing Azure committed spend to it. Read the Azure Marketplace documentation to learn how to take advantage of the Microsoft Azure consumption commitment (MACC) and Azure commit to consume (CtC).

Atlas supports paying for usage via the Google Cloud Marketplace (GCP MP) without any upfront commitment. You can link an Atlas account to a Google Cloud Billing Account, as well as delete an existing subscription.

MACC is a contractual commitment customers make with Microsoft to spend a specific amount on Azure over time. Customers can contribute to their MACC by purchasing MACC eligible third-party solutions in Microsoft Marketplace.
Google Cloud Marketplace expands with improved partner economics, simplified commit drawdown, and new incentives to drive cloud workload growth.

Atlas GCP Marketplace billing (listing 'MongoDB Atlas (Pay as You Go)') has no upfront commitment. An admin picks a Google Cloud Billing Account at subscription, then links an Atlas organization; outstanding or failed invoices must be resolved first. While linked, the payment method shows 'GCP Marketplace Subscription' and cannot be edited; removing it requires unlinking the billing account. Cancelling is done in GCP under Your Orders.

Starting June 9, all qualifying software purchases through Google Cloud Marketplace Channel Private Offers (MCPO) will result in a 100 percent commit drawdown tied to the final price on the private offer.
For an offer to be enrolled in MACC, it must meet all Azure IP Co-sell eligibility requirements. Once these requirements are met, you can expect your offer to be enrolled in MACC within 1 week.

Third party software routed through the marketplace draws down the commitment, which turns existing software renewals into commitment fuel. Buyers who modeled this hit drawdown milestones 2 to 3 quarters earlier than planned, using private offers that preserve their negotiated software pricing.

The Edit button in the Payment Method field is disabled when you have a GCP Marketplace Subscription. To remove the GCP Marketplace Subscription payment method, you must unlink your GCP Billing Account from MongoDB.

If you are already signed in to an existing MongoDB Atlas account, you are automatically redirected to the Select an Organization to Link to Your GCP Billing Account page on the MongoDB Atlas website when you click Register With MongoDB.

If you are not already signed in to an existing MongoDB Atlas account, you are prompted to sign in to a MongoDB Atlas account. After you sign-in, you are automatically redirected to the Select an Organization to Link to Your GCP Billing Account page.
On the Offer overview page, in the Marketplace programs section, the Microsoft Azure consumption commitment status shows either Enrolled or Not Enrolled.
Route third party software through the marketplace using private offers, which preserve your negotiated software pricing while the spend counts toward drawdown.

The sequencing rule is absolute: rightsize, schedule and clean up first, then forecast, then commit. Reversing it hands your optimization upside to the vendor, because every efficiency you find after signing becomes breakage risk rather than saving. Test the result before agreeing to it: model the commitment at 85 percent delivery, and if the penalty math frightens you, the commitment is too big. The asymmetry favors committing low, since overage at your negotiated rate is a much cheaper failure than breakage on an oversized commitment. You can always spend more. You can rarely unspend.

Since 2025-06-09, Google Cloud Marketplace Channel Private Offers (purchases through a Google-authorized channel partner) draw down at 100% of the private offer's final price, but the amount applied to the customer's minimum commitment is capped at 25%.

In addition, we are announcing that starting June 9, 2025, all qualifying software purchases through Google Cloud Marketplace Channel Private Offers (MCPO) will result in 100% commit drawdown tied to the final price on the private offer. This change simplifies our channel commit drawdown policy for purchases made through a Google-authorized channel partner and enables the full qualifying amount of the private offer (up to an allowable 25% cap) to be applied to the customer’s minimum commitment obligations.

Atlas docs list Marketplace as a distinct subscription type: invoices for usage come from the marketplace the customer subscribed through, not from MongoDB. The self-serve GCP page does not cover commitment drawdown, private offers, or changing the linked billing account.

Microsoft MACC eligibility is per offer: each Marketplace offer must be enrolled (Partner Center shows Enrolled/Not Enrolled), free and BYOL offers are not eligible, and only licenses used exclusively in Azure contribute. Atlas clusters deployed on non-Azure clouds are therefore a risk for MACC credit; the Atlas page does not address this.

Google excludes Marketplace services not running on Google Cloud from drawdown, and Google defers to the vendor on which services run on Google Cloud. For Atlas, clusters on AWS or Azure billed through the GCP Marketplace listing may therefore not count; this is an inference, and no Atlas or Google source states it for Atlas.

facts.text: Please note that MACC enrollment applies at the offer level. If you create multiple Marketplace offers, even for the same product, each offer must be MACC-eligible for the purchase to contribute to your customer's MACC.

The following services and software sold using Google Cloud Marketplace are excluded from commitment drawdown eligibility; any spend on such services or software won't count toward Minimum Commitment obligations:

The MACC benefit only applies to licenses that are exclusively used in Azure. If the license is deployed in a hybrid environment or on-premises, the purchased license is not eligible to contribute to your customer's MACC.
Free and BYOL (bring your own license) offers are NOT considered transactable and therefore do not meet IP Co-sell eligibility requirements or MACC requirements.

The standard account team pitch is to commit big, because a larger commitment unlocks a deeper discount band. We disagree. Across roughly 30 to 45 Google Cloud commitments Fredrik Filipsson benchmarked between 2024 and 2025, the recurring loss was over commitment, not under discounting: commits sized on the forward forecast overshot consumption by 18 to 28 percent of contract value, and the extra band never covered the unconsumed commit.
